Cloudflare's (NYSE:NET) stock seemed to be aiming for the clouds on Monday. Investors were still piling into the shares of the cloud connectivity and cybersecurity specialist after it reported its third-quarter figures on Thursday. This bullish sentiment was bolstered by a price target raise set over the weekend by an analyst covering the company.

Demand helps drive double-digit gains

That analyst, Piper Sandler's (NYSE:PIPR) James Fish, increased his fair value assessment on Cloudflare to $337 per share from $333. With this change, he maintained his overweight (i.e., buy) recommendation on the stock.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Cloudflare's third-quarter revenue was $782.5 million, 39% higher than its take for the same quarter of 2025. Net income not under generally accepted accounting principles (non-GAAP, or adjusted) came in at slightly under $144 million, or $0.38 per share. That metric's growth rate was 40%.

Both metrics beat the consensus estimates of analysts like Fish.

Artificial intelligence, real fears

Cloudflare also provided guidance for its current (fourth) quarter and the entirety of 2026. For the year, it expects revenue to total around $2.96 billion. Adjusted earnings per share (EPS) should be $1.35. If achieved, both figures would be notably above the 2025 results of $2.17 billion and $0.93, respectively.

Cybersecurity services are particularly popular these days, given the growing fear that "rogue" artificial intelligence (AI) models could be destructive to all manner of IT systems. The companies that can not only take advantage of this trend but also maximize it should continue to attract investors. Cloudflare is one of those companies.

title: Cloudflare's best quarter ever hit with a growing margin challenge
detail:
Cloudflare's best quarter ever hit with a growing margin challenge
Mwangi Enos
Mon, November 9, 2026 at 4:33 PM CST 5 min read
NET
Trade NET on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

I know you spend some time online, moving between sites and other websites. And I'm certain that now and then, a page has asked you to confirm you're human before letting you through. You might see it as a small interruption, but it shows how much work goes on behind the scenes to keep websites accessible while filtering out automated traffic.

You see that check? Often happens through Cloudflare, which serves 115 million web requests a second on average from data centers in more than 340 cities. And there's a reason. 

Imperva's 2026 Bad Bot Report found automated programs generated a record 53% of requests over the past year, with bad bots alone accounting for 40%. Another tally shows daily AI-enabled bot attacks rose from 2 million to 25 million in 2025 — a 12.5x year-over-year increase.

CEO Matthew Prince said the third quarter was "Cloudflare's best quarter ever," as revenue crossed a $3 billion annualized pace at $782.5 million, up 39%. It is its fastest growth in nearly four years. However, growing this fast has a price.

We have built the development platform for the AI-powered Internet—and as digital threats escalate, organizations of every size continue to rely on Cloudflare for protection.

Also Read: AI agents are quietly rewriting how the internet works

Cloudflare posts a record quarter, and Morgan Stanley stays bullish

In a note Morgan Stanley shared with me at TheStreet, it maintained an Overweight rating and a $370 price target on Cloudflare (NET). That's a 37% increase from Nov. 6 close of $268.75, according to Yahoo Finance. The bank said broad-based execution and momentum in developer and security products support durable growth. 

In fact, revenue beat Cloudflare's own guidance midpoint by $46 million, or 6.2%, and was more than 6% above consensus, while contracted future revenue grew 37%. Fourth-quarter guidance of $845-$846 million implies 38% growth, about 6% above consensus.

More AI:

Bank of America has unexpected verdict on AI stocks after post-midterm Democrat sweep

BofA cuts to the chase on AI data center demand

Cloudflare CEO disagrees with Bezos on AI and US jobs

Profits are catching up. Non-GAAP operating margin hit a record 17.5%, up 2.2 points. Non-GAAP EPS was $0.38 versus $0.27 a year ago. Cloudflare now expects GAAP profitability in the fourth quarter, well ahead of its previous 2028 target. In the third quarter, it still had a GAAP operating loss of $67.9 million.

All of that performance is reflected in its shares, which are up 36.32% this year, 18.97% over one year and 325.84% over three years through Nov. 6, according to Yahoo Finance.

What's driving Cloudflare's growth

Customers are arriving in huge numbers. In its Q3 earnings call, Cloudflare CEO said they added more than 158,000 paying customers, about double its prior quarterly record, lifting the total 110% from a year ago. It also added a record 308 large customers paying over $100,000 a year, bringing that group to about 5,000. 

Net retention rose 2 points to 122%, meaning existing customers are spending more. Sales productivity set a record for the 11th straight quarter, and quota attainment was the highest in more than five years.

Related: Canva CEO apologizes to workers, makes unusual promise amid layoffs

Much of the upside came from customers using more than expected. Under Cloudflare's pool-of-funds contracts, customers commit a budget and draw it down. They consumed faster, renewed earlier, and signed bigger commitments. Developers building on its Workers platform grew to more than 10 million from more than 7 million last quarter.

I see this as part of a broader shift in how people use the internet. Even a small website or online business needs reliable infrastructure to handle visitors, protect its pages, and keep everything running smoothly. And of course, as more services move online, the demand for the technology behind them keeps growing.

Security is another driver. AI-driven vulnerability discovery is raising urgency, and Cloudflare is winning more often against core zero-trust vendors. Management said security is playing a bigger role in expansion.

Cloudflare added more than 158,000 paying customers, about double its prior Q2 record, lifting the total 110% from a year ago.Smith Collection/Gado / Getty Images
The trade-offs Morgan Stanley is watching

Gross margin fell 0.7 points from the prior quarter and 2.9 points from a year ago to 72.4%, because the lower-margin developer platform is growing faster than the rest. Network capital spending stays at 14% to 15% of revenue as AI workloads and agent traffic grow. Management points to better compute efficiency.

Faster consumption also adds quarterly swings. And Christian Smith takes over as President of Revenue as Mark Anderson retires, just as sales execution peaks, which Morgan Stanley says could add risk in 2027. A new business line, Act IV, recorded its first revenue, including AI crawling, with agent access and micro-payments possible later. Timing and size remain uncertain.

For the full year, Cloudflare guides to revenue of about $2.96 billion, up 37%. Fourth-quarter non-GAAP operating income of $156 million to $157 million and EPS of $0.43 should follow.

So, Morgan Stanley's view is that growth broad enough to head toward 40% or more into 2027 outweighs those costs, as Cloudflare becomes a platform where app development, security, and AI agent traffic meet. Now, the things to watch are gross margin and the sales handoff.

Key Takeaways

Cloudflare fell 32% from its Oct. 9 record close to its Nov. 5 close, just before its third-quarter report. After the report, Goldman Sachs kept its Buy rating and $420 price target, 56% above the Nov. 6 close.

Revenue grew 39% in the third quarter, the fastest in nearly four years, and management now expects a GAAP profit in the fourth quarter.

Heading into the report, the consensus price target had risen to $345 from $240 a year ago, and analysts' 2027 earnings estimate had risen to $1.69 a share from $1.59 three months earlier.

Goldman's $420 works out to 284x forward earnings, well above any quarter-end multiple since mid-2023, so the Street's $345 average is the more realistic target for the next year.

Cloudflare (NET:NYSE) fell 32% from its Oct. 9 record close of $360.93 to $244.51 on Nov. 5, the day of its third-quarter report. Then it reported 39% revenue growth, its fastest in nearly four years, and shares rose 9.91% to $268.75 on Nov. 6. Goldman Sachs reiterated its Buy rating and $420 price target, 56% above that close.

A rough few weeks for AI stocks

A software selloff hit cloud stocks in late October. Then Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress after a campaign in which candidates from both parties went after AI data centers. And on Nov. 5, hours before the report, cybersecurity stocks sold off again as the AI trade unwound.

Goldman's case rests on the guide

Goldman's Gabriela Borges stuck with her call on Nov. 6, and the numbers gave her plenty to work with. Third-quarter revenue of $782.5 million beat Wall Street's $738.5 million estimate by 6%. The fourth-quarter outlook of $845 million to $846 million sits 6% above the Street on revenue, and the 43-cent adjusted EPS guide runs 13% ahead, based on consensus figures compiled by Benzinga. CEO Matthew Prince called it "Cloudflare's best quarter ever."

Cloudflare also expects a GAAP profit in that quarter. CFO Thomas Seifert said that would come "significantly earlier" than the 2028 deadline the company set at its investor day. It is a forecast, not a result yet.

Stacey Cunningham, who Bullish says was the first woman to lead NYSE Group, the company behind the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE), is the new president of crypto exchange operator Bullish, the company announced on Monday. She stepped into that NYSE role in 2018 as the successor to Tom Farley, now Bullish's chief executive, who had run NYSE Group since 2014.

The announcement did not give a start date, a reporting line or pay terms. Farley said in the release that Cunningham "will play a central role in building the next generation of services for market participants," and called her "one of the most respected leaders in global capital markets."

Cunningham has advised Uniswap Labs, the developer behind the Uniswap trading protocol, and sits on the boards of the NYSE, Cloudflare and a Georgetown University financial markets center. Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), the NYSE's parent, named Lynn Martin to succeed her as president in December 2021. Before she became president, Cunningham was the NYSE's chief operating officer, and Bullish credits her senior roles there with overseeing the modernization of the exchange's technology and folding several acquired exchanges into its operations. Earlier on, she worked in senior positions at Nasdaq.

Get Unchained's crypto news in your inbox with the free Unchained Daily newsletter.

Why an Exchange Veteran

Farley tied the hire to Cunningham's "relationships with issuers built over decades." He has made the same pitch for Equiniti, the company Bullish is acquiring: in July he said bringing together its "deep-rooted issuer relationships" and its business keeping companies' official shareholder registers with Bullish's blockchain-native platform "creates something that doesn't exist today."

The Equiniti Deal

Bullish agreed on May 5 to buy Equiniti for $4.2 billion: $1.85 billion of Equiniti debt that Bullish will assume plus roughly $2.35 billion in Bullish shares. At the $38.48 per-share price the deal set, that stock portion works out to about 61 million Bullish shares, by Unchained's math. Siris, which is selling Equiniti, will receive two board seats under the deal, Bullish said. Equiniti is a transfer agent, the firm a public company pays to keep its official register of who owns its stock, and Bullish says Equiniti counts nearly 3,000 issuers as clients. In July, Bullish said it had received competition clearances in the U.K., the U.S. and Germany, with other approvals still pending and closing expected in January 2027.

When the deal was announced in May, Farley framed the purchase around tokenization (recording securities such as stocks on blockchains), which he called "a once-in-a-generation shift in how capital markets operate." Regulators in Gibraltar have approved Bullish for tokenized securities trading, and tokenized versions of Bullish's own stock, issued with the company's backing, already trade. Bullish owns the crypto news outlet CoinDesk.

Cloudflare (NET) has been one of the most searched-for stocks on Zacks.com lately. So, you might want to look at some of the facts that could shape the stock's performance in the near term.

Over the past month, shares of this web security and content delivery company have returned -25.5%, compared to the Zacks S&P 500 composite's -5.6% change. During this period, the Zacks Internet - Software industry, which Cloudflare falls in, has lost 13.4%. The key question now is: What could be the stock's future direction?

Although media reports or rumors about a significant change in a company's business prospects usually cause its stock to trend and lead to an immediate price change, there are always certain fundamental factors that ultimately drive the buy-and-hold decision.

Revisions to Earnings Estimates

Here at Zacks, we prioritize appraising the change in the projection of a company's future earnings over anything else. That's because we believe the present value of its future stream of earnings is what determines the fair value for its stock.

We essentially look at how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to reflect the impact of the latest business trends. And if earnings estimates go up for a company, the fair value for its stock goes up. A higher fair value than the current market price drives investors' interest in buying the stock, leading to its price moving higher. This is why empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

Cloudflare is expected to post earnings of $0.38 per share for the current quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +35.7%. Over the last 30 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate remained unchanged.

For the current fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $1.27 points to a change of +36.6% from the prior year. Over the last 30 days, this estimate has changed +2.7%.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $1.73 indicates a change of +36.4% from what Cloudflare is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed +0.6%.

With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool -- the Zacks Rank -- is a more conclusive indicator of a stock's near-term price performance, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) for Cloudflare.

Rising Cyber Threats to Boost Cloudflare's Security Growth

Cloudflare is seeing rising demand for its cybersecurity offerings as businesses face an increase in Internet vulnerabilities and evolving cyber threats. The growing use of AI is helping security researchers identify vulnerabilities faster, increasing the need for stronger protection.

During its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, management highlighted that six of the most serious Internet security vulnerabilities had been disclosed in less than 14 days. Cloudflare said it receives early disclosures of vulnerabilities from major AI labs and security companies and puts protections in place for its customers before these issues become public. StockStory's take

Cloudflare's third quarter saw strong business momentum, with results ahead of Wall Street expectations and a significant positive market reaction. Management attributed the outperformance to rapid expansion across customer segments, citing a record increase in large customer wins and robust adoption of the Workers Developer Platform. CEO Matthew Prince highlighted that the acceleration was not limited to AI-native companies but included broad growth across industries such as financial services, government, and e-commerce. The company also benefited from improved sales productivity and a surge in new paying customers.

Looking ahead, Cloudflare's raised guidance is underpinned by management's view that the company's platform is well positioned for continued adoption in an environment increasingly shaped by AI-driven workloads and evolving internet security needs. CFO Thomas Seifert emphasized that expanded pool of funds contracts and faster customer usage are boosting recurring revenue visibility. Management believes that advancements in agent-based computing and increasing security threats will further drive demand for Cloudflare's services, with Prince stating, "Cloudflare is at the center of defining what the agentic internet is going to look like."
